label: rem:hochschild-kummer-connection
title: The Hochschild--Kummer connection
html:
The Kummer filtration of H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) maps to the Hochschild cohomology of the Frobenius–Hopf algebra A via the Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg comparison:

  HH^2(\mathcal{U}_q, \mathrm{Ad})
  \xrightarrow{ \mathrm{HKR}}
  H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m).

The deformation-theoretic obstruction (Hochschild) and the gerbe-theoretic obstruction (Yekutieli) present two views of the same class. The Kummer filtration pulls back to a filtration on HH^2 measuring the n-divisibility of deformation obstructions [yekutieli2010].

Motivic-Galois interpretation. The Kummer filtration on H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m) restricts the motivic-Galois filtration to the cyclotomic subgroup \mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\mu_\infty)/\mathbb{Q}). Under the motivic substrate realization tower \{\rho_v\}, the Hochschild class \kappa \in HH^2(\mathcal{U}_q, \mathrm{Ad}) projects at each finite place p to a motivic Chern class \rho_p(\kappa) \in H^1_{\mathrm{Gal}}(\mathrm{Gal}(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}_p/\mathbb{Q}_p), \mu_n(1)) through the cyclotomic ideal \mathbb{Z}[q]/\Phi_n(q). Perpetual non-vanishing of \kappa_n at every finite place p \nmid \chi(A) (Kummer tower, Descartes Yekutieli) means the motivic Galois character of the Frobenius–Hopf substrate is non-trivial in \mathrm{Hom}(\chi_n, 1) for almost every n. The HKR comparison bridges the gerbe (geometric) and Hochschild (deformation) realizations of this single motivic class.
